ceilingSources.residentMemoryBytes: rule: 2x the larger measured resident set (62046208 B over the recorded hosts), rounded up to a whole MiB; evidence runtime-budget.evidence/
ceilingSources.idleCpuPercent: rule: 1 percent absolute for an idle crate; measured at most 0.053 percent on the recorded hosts
ceilingSources.wakeupsPerSecond: rule: max(1, 2x the largest recorded 0.3.2 release-iterate whole-process idle rate), rounded up to 0.1/s: ceil(10 * max(1, 2 * max(5.089, 4.859))) / 10 = 10.2/s. Workload: default watchdog on an idle Wry event loop with no windows, 5 s warm-up, 30 s observation. macOS measures process interrupt wake-ups; Windows measures live-thread context-switch totals as a proxy. Includes heartbeat-induced main-thread dispatch and native runtime activity; not a watchdog-thread-only design bound. Evidence: runtime-budget.evidence/darwin-arm64-0.3.2-synthetic.txt and win32-x64-0.3.2-synthetic.txt.
ceilingSources.diskOpsPerSecond: design bound: the watchdog threads touch only atomics, the wake bell and the callback (src/watchdog.rs module doc), so the crate issues no disk operations; 1 per second absolute, the sibling crates' floor. Windows measures it (GetProcessIoCounters); macOS exposes no per-process disk-operation counter

status.note: The status call returns rightkit_child_process::ProcessUsage (resident and footprint bytes, cumulative CPU seconds, and whole-process wake-up and disk-operation totals where the host reports them: macOS interrupt wake-ups, Windows live-thread context switches as a wake-up proxy, disk operations on Windows and Linux); the rates come from two calls (ProcessUsage::rates_since).

notes: Ceilings come from the recorded measurements by stated rules (ceilingSources); a ceiling left null names its reason below. wakeupsPerSecond is derived from the 0.3.2 whole-process measurements on both hosts; diskOpsPerSecond is a design bound (see ceilingSources); macOS exposes no per-process disk-operation counter.
